finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to fopen without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink function is fopen, which only opens a file and does not invoke a shell or execute commands. OS Command Injection requires a function that passes data to a shell (e.g., system, execve, popen). Since fopen merely resolves a pathname and opens the file, no command injection is possible. The reported trigger about shell metacharacters or path traversal does not lead to command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to fread without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported sink is fread, which simply reads data from an already opened FILE pointer. fread does not invoke a shell or execute any command, so it cannot be used for OS command injection. The only place where the untrusted filename is used is in fopen, which opens a file but does not spawn a command. Therefore the claim of command injection is unfounded.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to gcry_sexp_new without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported OS Command Injection claim is unfounded because the sink function gcry_sexp_new does not execute shell commands; it merely parses the provided data into an S-expression. The untrusted source "filename" is only used in fopen (lines 9‑13) to open a file, and the file contents are read into memory and passed to gcry_sexp_new (line 35). No command string is constructed or passed to a shell, so there is no path from the filename to a command execution. Therefore the vulnerability is a false positive.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to free without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code for any data flow from the untrusted source 'filename' to the sink 'free'. The only use of 'filename' is in fopen (line 9). The variable 'filecontent' is allocated with malloc (line 21) and freed at line 36. There is no assignment or copy of 'filename' into 'filecontent', nor any string manipulation that would propagate shell metacharacters to the memory freed. Additionally, 'free' is not an OS command execution function, so it cannot be a vector for command injection. Therefore, no path exists from the untrusted source to the sink, and the reported vulnerability is invalid.
